findings.message: This reported account is correctly marked as private internal grounding and excluded from public deliverables. Keep that boundary: the transcript assertion is not independent verification, and anonymity would not clear public reuse.
The reported Orlando-first plan and possible later Colorado targeting are accurately qualified as private intentions, not completed work. Do not expose them publicly without permission review.

The public teaching route is framed as conditional inference, avoids the private account and market names, and preserves the possibility of a coherent shared page. No performance outcome is claimed; retain the direction to validate differences rather than infer preferences from geography.

The exact approved CTA survives. Because “for a better client experience” could read as an established benefit, keep the required adjacent, readable caveat in every standalone deliverable stating that venue-level tailoring is untested and no measured client-experience result is supplied.

The similarity review explicitly admits that the legacy publication catalogue is missing. The supplied prior arguments are pending and have no publications listed, so the substantive distinctions support differentiation from those arguments—not a claim of publication novelty or comprehensive archive coverage.
